sources.title: The Organization and Operation of Inferior Temporal Cortex
sources.coverage: IT cortex organizational model (4-stage framework); eccentricity templates; face patches as canonical operations; color as behavioral relevance signal; evolutionary replication hypothesis
key_facts_used: IT organized along posterior-anterior axis into PIT/CIT/AIT/AMIT stages
Each stage has foveal (face), mid-periphery (color/relevance), peripheral (scene) representations
Face patches are manifestations of canonical IT operations, not unique modules
Color processing signals behavioral relevance (ripeness, blood), not identity per se
Experience (face exposure) required for face patch development

sources.title: Functional compartmentalization and viewpoint generalization within the macaque face-processing system
sources.coverage: Macaque face patch hierarchy; view-specific to view-invariant gradient; single-neuron recordings from ML/MF/AL/AM
key_facts_used: 6 face patches total: PL, ML, MF, AF, AL, AM
ML/MF: 97% face selectivity, highly view-specific
AL: 86% face selectivity, mirror-symmetric tuning for partial view invariance
AM: 89% face selectivity, 73% identity-modulated, near-complete view invariance
Posterior-to-anterior gradient: view-specific → view-invariant

sources.title: Balanced increases in selectivity and tolerance produce constant sparseness along the ventral visual stream
sources.coverage: Selectivity vs. tolerance tradeoff; sparseness conservation along V4→IT; quantitative comparison of natural image response rates
key_facts_used: V4 sparseness: ~11% of natural images trigger >50% peak firing
IT sparseness: ~9.4% (no significant difference from V4)
Selectivity (and-like operations) and tolerance (or-like operations) both increase from V4 to IT
Balanced increases maintain constant sparseness
Sparseness ~10% may represent optimal information-energy tradeoff

sources.title: Visual Functions of Primate Area V4
sources.authors: Pasupathy A, Popovkina DV, Kim T
sources.coverage: V4 shape selectivity in object-centered coordinates; boundary conformation tuning; real vs. accidental contours; response latencies; multi-feature joint tuning
key_facts_used: V4 neurons tuned for boundary curvature × object-centered angular position
Mean response latency: 76.6 ms (range 25-200 ms)
V4 distinguishes real object boundaries from accidental occlusion contours
V4 shows joint tuning for shape + texture + color + depth
Position invariance begins to emerge in V4

sources.title: Unsupervised neural network models of the ventral visual stream
sources.authors: Zhuang C, Yan S, Nayebi A, Schrimpf M, Frank MC, DiCarlo JJ, Yamins DLK
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
sources.coverage: Unsupervised DNN comparison to primate ventral stream; contrastive embedding methods; infant visual data training
key_facts_used: Contrastive embedding unsupervised DNNs match or exceed supervised models in predicting V4/IT responses
Models trained on real infant head-camera video still produce brain-like representations
Supports biologically plausible computational theory of visual learning (no labeled data needed)

sources.title: Does the brain's ventral visual pathway compute object shape?
sources.coverage: Challenge to ventral stream = shape computation; texform evidence; dorsal stream shape hypothesis
key_facts_used: Texforms (texture-reconstructed unrecognizable images) activate similar topographic IT organization as real objects
Scrambling spatial feature arrangement: humans detect difference, IT/DNN do not
Proposal: dorsal pathway computes global shape/skeletal structure; ventral = local feature statistics
This creates a contested claim relative to classical ventral stream = shape recognition view

sources.title: Neuronal Mechanisms Underlying Face Recognition in Non-human Primates
sources.authors: Amita H, Koyano KW, Kunimatsu J
sources.coverage: NHP face recognition neural mechanisms; face patch network updates; connections to subcortical and frontal areas
key_facts_used: Face patches identified in early 2000s as breakthrough in primate face recognition research
Face processing network includes temporal cortex, frontal areas, striatum, amygdala
Different patches specialize in feature analysis, identity categorization, social familiarity, memory

sources.coverage: Distributed face/object representation; even non-face-preferred regions carry face category information
